faq: What kind of problems can you fix?

Broken links, missing images, wrong prices or stock, product options that came across badly, forms that do not send and pages that look wrong. Problems with a platform's own limits are explained, with options.
How soon after launch should I order this?
About one to two weeks after the move works best, when enough shoppers have used the store to show patterns. If something urgent breaks earlier, tell us, and we can look at it right away.
Do I need to list the problems?
A list helps but is not required. Send what you or your customers noticed, and we run our own scans for the rest. The more detail you share, the faster we can reach the cause.
What if the problem comes from the old data?
We trace it back to the source. If the old store had errors, we fix the new copy and tell you what was wrong, so you do not carry the same mistake into other tools.

desc:
Post-migration fixes and cleanup deal with the problems that appear once real customers use your moved store. Ecom Swift LLC collects what has gone wrong, fixes issues at the cause and reports what changed, so the new store settles down quickly.

## What are post-migration fixes?

Post-migration fixes are the repairs made in the weeks after a store moves to a new platform. Even a careful migration leaves small faults: a product with a missing image, a link that leads nowhere, an email that never arrives, a total that differs from the old store.

This service is a focused cleanup. You bring the list of problems, or we find them with scans, and we work through them in order.

## Why the first weeks after launch matter

Testing uses a few people and a few paths. Live traffic uses thousands of paths at once, on every device and browser. That is why the first days bring support emails about things nobody predicted.

Left alone, small faults add up. Broken links waste search visits, odd product data confuses buyers and unanswered complaints make customers wonder whether the store is reliable. A quick, organized cleanup keeps the good impression the new store was meant to give.

## How cleanup affects sales and search

Each fault has a cost. A product page with the wrong image sells less. A collection that returns an error loses its visitors. A form that does not deliver loses a lead. Fixing these returns the lost orders and enquiries you would otherwise never know you missed.

Search visibility also needs attention. After a move, search engines report pages they cannot reach or that redirect badly. Working through those reports helps pages return to results, though timing depends on how often search engines revisit your site.

## What a good cleanup covers

- A review of every problem you have noticed or customers have reported.
- A scan for broken links across the whole store.
- Review of search error pages and the fixes they need.
- Product data checked: titles, prices, variants, images and descriptions.
- Image problems repaired, such as missing, stretched or oversized files.
- Totals for orders and customers compared with the old store.
- Email and form delivery checked, including spam folder behavior.
- Mobile layout problems corrected.
- Speed review for heavy pages.
- A short report of what was found, what was changed and what needs your decision.

## What we do

We start with your list and with our own scans of the live store. We group the findings by cause, since many visible problems come from one underlying fault, such as a wrong setting or a bad import field. Fixing the cause clears them all.

We then work through the list in order of impact. The Basic package covers the most urgent items and a link scan. Standard adds a larger set of fixes, search error work, product data repair and a check of totals. Premium includes a second review after a few days of real traffic, email and form checks and a prioritized list for the following month.

Where a problem comes from the old data, we tell you and suggest what can be done.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep a running list of customer complaints.
- Note the page, device and time when you spot a fault.
- Check the search tool's error report weekly.
- Keep your old store data available for comparison.
- Fix the most visible problems first.

**Avoid:**
- Hiding errors with quick patches.
- Changing many settings at once.
- Ignoring emails that say a message never arrived.
- Waiting months before reporting a fault.
- Deleting the old export before the cleanup ends.

## Who this is for

An owner who has just launched and keeps finding small errors. A team that tested well but lacks time to chase every detail. A seller whose support inbox suddenly includes questions about missing products or odd prices.

## What we need from you

Send a list of problems, even a rough one, plus any customer messages that describe them. Give us staff or collaborator access to the new store and, if you can, view access to your search tool.

We never ask for passwords. Where a fix needs an action only you can take, such as approving a setting with your provider, we explain it step by step.
